title: Gallery
text: plot_oncoprint() plot_waterfall() function two names used different communities — “oncoprint” ComplexHeatmap/ cBioPortal vocabulary, “waterfall plot” GenVisR/maftools vocabulary. waterfall plot oncoprint visualisation: plot_waterfall() plot_oncoprint() aliases one function produce identical output — use whichever name field uses. bundled example VCF two samples, show cascade staircase plot built around. cohort illustrative synthetic data generated just article (package’s example data), sized like real cohort staircase annotation track visible, clinical stage track added via annotation:
code: set.seed(42)  genes <- c("TP53", "KRAS", "PIK3CA", "EGFR", "BRCA1",            "BRCA2", "APC", "PTEN", "ARID1A", "SMAD4") gene_freq <- c(TP53 = 0.85, KRAS = 0.55, PIK3CA = 0.40, EGFR = 0.30,                BRCA1 = 0.22, BRCA2 = 0.18, APC = 0.14, PTEN = 0.10,                ARID1A = 0.07, SMAD4 = 0.05) samples <- sprintf("COHORT_S%02d", 1:28) consequences <- c("missense_variant", "stop_gained",                    "frameshift_variant", "synonymous_variant")  cohort <- do.call(rbind, lapply(genes, function(g) {   n_mut <- max(1, round(gene_freq[[g]] * length(samples)))   data.frame(     chrom = "chr1", pos = sample(1e6:2e6, n_mut),     ref = "A", alt = "T", gene = g,     sample = sample(samples, n_mut),     consequence = sample(consequences, n_mut, replace = TRUE),     stringsAsFactors = FALSE   ) })) cohort_variants <- coerce_variants(cohort)  clinical_stage <- data.frame(   sample = samples,   stage  = sample(c("I", "II", "III", "IV"), length(samples), replace = TRUE) )  plot_waterfall(cohort_variants, top_n = 10, annotation = clinical_stage)

title: Getting started with ggvariant
text: read_vcf() parses standard VCF v4.x files — including gzipped files multi-sample VCFs — returns tidy data frame called gvf object. Functional annotations SnpEff (ANN) VEP (CSQ) INFO fields extracted automatically. result plain data frame one row per variant per sample, columns chromosome, position, alleles, consequence, gene, sample name. standard data frame, can filter, subset, manipulate R tools already know.
code: vcf_file <- system.file("extdata", "example.vcf", package = "ggvariant") variants  <- read_vcf(vcf_file) #> ℹ Reading VCF: example.vcf #> ✔ Reading VCF: example.vcf [58ms] #>  #> Loaded 19 variant records across 7 chromosomes.  head(variants) #> <gvf: 6 variants, 1 sample, 3 chromosomes, 4 genes> #>   chrom      pos ref alt qual filter        consequence  gene   sample #> 1 chr17  7577120   C   T  250   PASS   missense_variant  TP53 TUMOR_S1 #> 3 chr17  7578210   G   T   95   PASS        stop_gained  TP53 TUMOR_S1 #> 4 chr17  7579472   A   G  310   PASS synonymous_variant  TP53 TUMOR_S1 #> 6 chr13 32914437   G   A  175   PASS frameshift_variant BRCA2 TUMOR_S1 #> 7 chr17 41244000  AT   A  310   PASS frameshift_variant BRCA1 TUMOR_S1 #> 9  chr7 55242465   C   A   90   PASS synonymous_variant  EGFR TUMOR_S1

title: Getting started with ggvariant
text: Overlaying known protein domains helps interpret variants fall functionally. Provide data frame name, start, end columns (amino acid coordinates):
code: tp53_domains <- data.frame(   name  = c("Transactivation", "DNA-binding", "Tetramerization"),   start = c(1,   102, 323),   end   = c(67,  292, 356) )  # Scale genomic positions to protein coordinates tp53 <- variants[variants$gene == "TP53", ] tp53$pos <- round(   (tp53$pos - min(tp53$pos)) /   (max(tp53$pos) - min(tp53$pos)) * 393 ) + 1  plot_lollipop(tp53, gene = "TP53",               domains        = tp53_domains,               protein_length = 393)

title: Related work
text: vcfR (Knaus & Grünwald 2017) VariantAnnotation (Obenchain et al. 2014) read VCF files R predate ggvariant ten years. vcfR represents VCF S4 vcfR object base R plotting methods quality-control diagnostics coverage, depth, quality distributions; built around ggplot2 output data frame. VariantAnnotation part core Bioconductor variant-calling infrastructure: parses VCF VCF/CollapsedVCF objects built GRanges, designed interoperate rest Bioconductor’s genomic-ranges ecosystem (annotation lookups, overlap operations, reference genome access) rather produce plots directly. read_vcf() covers narrower slice job: returns plain tidy data frame (gvf object — data.frame added class attribute, nothing ), trading richer Bioconductor object model format dplyr/tidyr/base R workflow already knows manipulate, direct compatibility ggvariant’s plotting functions.

title: Related work
text: maftools (Mayakonda et al. 2018), GenVisR (Skidmore et al. 2016), ComplexHeatmap (Gu et al. 2016) provide oncoprint/waterfall-style summary plots, tracing back visualisation introduced cBioPortal (Gao et al. 2013; Cerami et al. 2012). maftools works MAF-format input tightly coupled cancer-genomics-specific data model. ComplexHeatmap’s oncoPrint() general-purpose heatmap infrastructure happens support oncoprint layout, cost larger, general API surface aimed heatmaps general, variant data specifically. plot_oncoprint() (aliased plot_waterfall()) implements memo-sort gene/sample ordering tools use, takes tidy gvf input every ggvariant function returns plain ggplot object, composes ggplot2 layers way rest package .

title: Related work
text: MutationalPatterns (Blokzijl et al. 2018) computes visualises mutational signatures full 96-class trinucleotide context (Alexandrov et al. 2020), including signature refitting reference catalogues, depends BSgenome reference-genome package extract context. plot_variant_spectrum() one narrower thing: plots unweighted 6-class single-base-substitution spectrum genome dependency. 96-class context support planned yet implemented (context/genome currently abort rather anything); , plot_variant_spectrum() substitute MutationalPatterns’ signature-analysis capability, simpler 6-class summary.

title: Related work
text: ggvariant’s distinguishing feature tools — several substantially . small API surface: read VCF file plain data frame, get back gvf tidy data frame, call one function per plot type, get back ordinary ggplot object. Bioconductor dependency bespoke S4 class learn. trade-real: less capability, exchange less learn full ggplot2 composability.

title: Oncoprint / waterfall plot of variants across samples — plot_oncoprint
text: Gene order. Genes ranked number distinct samples carrying least one mutation gene (ties broken total mutation count, alphabetically), top_n frequently altered genes shown, -altered top. Sample order. Samples ordered using memo-sort ("cascade") algorithm: displayed genes, already ranked --least altered, treated bits binary number (-altered gene significant bit). sample's mutation pattern across displayed genes scored binary number, samples sorted descending score (ties broken alphabetically sample name). greedily groups samples share mutations top genes together, producing characteristic left--right staircase pattern. displayed genes contribute score; genes excluded top_n/ genes effect sample order. Multi-hit cells. gene mutated sample represented single consequence colour, shown distinct "Multi_Hit" category instead either consequence.

title: ggvariant 0.2.0
text: Added plot_oncoprint() / plot_waterfall(): gene--sample mutation matrix (visualisation ComplexHeatmap/cBioPortal GenVisR/maftools community names, respectively). Genes ranked descending number altered samples; samples ordered memo-sort/cascade algorithm characteristic staircase pattern. Multi-hit cells (gene mutated one sample) render distinct "Multi_Hit" category. Supports optional clinical annotation track sample-metadata data frame. Suggested Nour-al-dain Marzouka (#N). Added plot_tmb(): per-sample tumour mutational burden bar chart, raw counts normalised mutations/Mb. read_vcf()’s gvf objects now real print.gvf() summary.gvf() methods, showing compact header consequence/ sample/chromosome breakdowns instead raw data.frame dump.

title: ggvariant 0.2.0
text: read_vcf() longer attaches variant homozygous-reference ("0/0") sample. .pivot_samples()’s presence check excluded literal missing-genotype codes, every sample pivoted carrying every variant regardless actual genotype multi-sample VCF. affected every per-sample dimension read_vcf()’s output: plot_lollipop(color_by = "sample"), plot_consequence_summary()’s per-sample bars, new sample-aware plots . Predates release entirely (present since 0.1.0) (#3). plot_variant_spectrum()’s context/genome arguments read_vcf()’s info_fields argument now abort informative error instead silently ignored. None three actually implemented, despite documented (#1, #2). VCF missing #CHROM header line, containing data line wrong number tab-separated fields, now aborts clear message instead failing deep inside opaque base-R error. nonexistent file path now aborts clear message instead normalizePath()’s base-R error.

title: ggvariant 0.2.0
text: read_vcf()’s .parse_ann_csq() (ANN/CSQ INFO field parsing) now vectorised whole INFO column instead looping row row. ~8.75x faster isolation synthetic 100,000-record VCF (8.05s -> 0.92s); full read_vcf() file drops 11.62s 3.68s.

title: ggvariant 0.2.0
text: Added pkgdown site. introductory vignette renamed ggvariant.Rmd activate “Get started” navbar convention, three new articles (Gallery, interactive plots, customising ggplot2) live vignettes/articles/ rather shipped vignettes, per R Packages’ guidance graphics-heavy content. Removed stray scratch files (Mutation 1.pdf, Rplot*.png/.pdf, etc.) shipping inside package tarball triggering R CMD check WARNING NOTE. Added R-CMD-check, test-coverage, pkgdown GitHub Actions workflows, fixed Codecov badge, pointed nonexistent main branch. Test coverage increased 68.12% 92%, including first tests malformed/edge-case input first vdiffr visual regression snapshots.

title: ggvariant 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-02-27 Initial CRAN release. read_vcf() coerce_variants() read VCF files plain data frames tidy gvf object. plot_lollipop(), plot_consequence_summary(), plot_variant_spectrum() provide ggplot2-native variant visualizations. gv_palette() theme_ggvariant() provide built-colour palettes shared plot theme.
